provenance.pipeline: Route 1: user-supplied textured GLB -> high-detail solid-color exterior -> agent-designed six-seat interior -> Blockbench Generic Model for the Minecraft Java Immersive Aircraft renderer; authored geometry is 1.5x the reconstruction and the data-pack skin applies its final world scale

identity_features: layered and framed black cockpit glazing
deep horizontal front grille and twin four-barrel utility thrusters
large white rescue module with six-spoke red medical marks and door latches
four teal faceted hover pods with vent arrays, white suspension guards, hubs, and dark pads
stepped rear service hatch with grooves, lower gray band, and teal bumper
roof hatch, emergency light modules, red beacon, and twin rear-leaning cyan-tip antennae
two forward cockpit bucket seats with dashboard displays
four rear passenger seats arranged in two rows
closed bilateral cargo doors with retained rear-edge hinge pivots
rear medical console and overhead cabin light
layered cargo-door frames with raised latches and amber edge markers
vented pod armor, segmented top pads, and layered diamond hub caps
six-bar front grille with paired utility nozzle clusters
segmented roof plating with four signal housings and antenna feet

subject.description: A six-occupant Minecraft-native armored hover ambulance with two cockpit seats, four rear passenger seats, an aisle, dashboard controls, and closed side cargo doors.
subject.intended_runtime: Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.1 through the Immersive Aircraft Blockbench model loader; the Bedrock geometry file is only an optional generated artifact
subject.seat_layout: two cockpit seats plus four rear seats in two forward-facing rows
uncertainties: The supplied GLB has no modeled interior, so the six-seat cabin is an inferred functional layout.
The data-pack skin scales the authored model to 16.32 blocks long and supplies matching final world-space seat positions.
Cargo doors are closed in the saved variant; their rear-edge hinge pivots are retained for later animation.
